Extra: 🦉 Maahmaahdu waa xikmad. (A proverb is wisdom.)

Somali: “Aqoon la’aani waa iftiin la’aan.” — Qofka aan aqoon lahayn wuxuu ku nool yahay mugdi; aqoontuna waa iftiin.
English: “Without knowledge there is no light.” — The ignorant live in darkness; knowledge is light.

Somali: “Nabad iyo caano.” — Salaan iyo duco qadiimi ah oo loo rajaynayo nabad iyo nolol wanaagsan.
English: “Peace and milk.” — An old greeting and blessing wishing peace and a good life.

Somali: Maahmaahyadu waxay ku kala duwan yihiin gobollada; waxaa loo baahan yahay in macallinku tusaalooyinka deegaanka ku daro.
English: Proverbs vary by region; teachers should add local examples.

Somali: Maahmaahdu waxay ku habboon tahay xaalad gaar ah: markaad talo siinayso, dood ka qayb qaadanayso, ama sheeko sheeganayso. Waxaa laga yaabaa in gobollada kala duwan si kala duwan loo dhigo — waa in la ixtiraamo kala duwanaanshaha.
English: A proverb fits a particular situation: giving advice, joining a discussion or telling a story. Wording varies between regions — respect that variation.
Extra: “Aqoon la’aani waa iftiin la’aan” — marka aan kuu sheego inaad wax barato. (Use it when urging someone to learn.)

Extra: 🖼️ Sawirku wuxuu ka dhigayaa erayga mid nool. (Imagery makes words come alive.)

Somali:
Dhulkaa baxaya, doobku wuu shaqayn,
Dadku wuu wada jiraa, wada jirkuna waa dar.
English:
The land blooms, the youth shall work,
The people stand together, and togetherness is strength.

Somali: (Tani waa tusaale macallin sameeyay, lagumana soo xigin gabay abwaan caan ah. Ujeeddadu waa in la barto sawirka, celceliska iyo laxanka.)
English: (This is an original teaching example, not quoted from a famous poet. Its purpose is to teach imagery, repetition and rhythm.)

Somali: Marka aad gabay akhrido: (1) erayada sawirka leh raadi, (2) celceliska iyo laxanka maqli, (3) mawduuca aqoonsan, (4) dareenka qoraa fahmo, (5) fikrad gaar ah oo salaysan qoraal ka dhis. Ha soo saarin sharaxaad aan la xaqiijin — u dhowaanshahaaga gaarka ah sheego.
English: When reading a poem: (1) find image words, (2) hear repetition and rhythm, (3) identify the theme, (4) feel the poet’s emotion, (5) build your own text-based interpretation. Never present an unverified interpretation as fact — state it as your reading.
Extra: Fikrad: “wada” waxay xoojisaa wadajirka. (Reading: “wada” emphasises togetherness.)

Somali: Dhinaca A: Waxbarashada casriga ah waxay isticmaashaa kombuyuutar iyo internet. Tani waxay fududeysaa barashada, waxayna keentaa xog badan.
English: Side A: Modern education uses computers and the internet. This eases learning and brings much information.

Somali: Dhinaca B: Tiknolojiyaddu waa mid waxtar leh, laakiin akhriska buugga iyo macallinka tooska ah waa saldhigga barashada. Carruurtu waxay u baahan yihiin waqti ay akhriyaan oo ay qoraan.
English: Side B: Technology is useful, but reading books and direct teaching are the foundation of learning. Children need time to read and write.

Somali: Gunaanadka macallinka: labada dhinacba waxay leeyihiin caddayn; wanaaggu wuxuu ku jiraa isku-darka.
English: Teacher’s conclusion: both sides have evidence; the good lies in combining them.

Somali: Dood ka qayb qaado: saddex caddayn keen oo jawaab bixi.
English: Join a debate: bring three pieces of evidence and respond.

⚖️ Xuquuqda qoraha waa la ixtiraamaa. (The author’s rights are respected.)

Somali: Maalin maalmaha ka mid ah, oday ayaa geed hoostiisa fadhiistay. Carruur ayaa u timid oo weydiisay: “Awoowe, maxay dadku u akhriyaan?” Odaygii wuxuu ugu jawaabay: “Ilmaha yar, geedku marka uu yar yahay waa la waraabiyaa, marka uu weynaadana wuxuu bixiyaa midho. Maskaxdu sidoo kale: haddii aad maanta akhrido, berri ayaad midho bixin doontaa.”
English: One day an elder sat under a tree. Children came and asked: “Grandfather, why do people read?” The elder answered: “Little ones, a tree is watered when small and gives fruit when grown. The mind is the same: if you read today, tomorrow you will give fruit.”

Somali: Carruurtii way farxeen oo maalintiias waxay bilaabeen inay akhriyaan.
English: The children were happy and that day they began to read.

Extra: answer: labaduba marka la daryeelo way baxaan

Somali: Suugaanta casriga ah (maansooyinka, riwaayadaha, sheekooyinka) waxaa leh abwaannada iyo qorayaasha. Waxaa la akhriyi karaa, laakiin laguma soo xigayo goobtan iyada oo aan oggolaansho lahayn. Sheekooyinka dhaqameedka ah iyo maahmaahyada waa dhaxal bulsho, waxaase weli lagu qoraa meesha laga keenay.
English: Modern literature belongs to its poets and writers. It may be read, but must not be quoted here without permission. Traditional folktales and proverbs are community heritage, yet sources should still be noted.
Extra: Haddii aad rabto inaad gabay soo xigto, oggolaansho haka qaado qoraha. (If you want to quote a poem, get permission from the poet.)

📰 Maqaal kooban ayaan qoray. (I wrote a short essay.)

Somali: Maqaalku wuxuu leeyahay saddex qayb: bilow (cinwaan iyo fikrad koowaad), jidh (saddex ama afar qaybood oo mid kasta leh fikrad iyo caddayn), iyo dhamaad (gunaanad). Warqadda rasmiga ah waxay leedahay: taariikhda, magaca qofka, cinwaanka, jidhka iyo saxiixa.
English: An essay has three parts: an introduction (title and first idea), a body (three or four paragraphs, each with an idea and evidence) and an ending (conclusion). A formal letter has: the date, the recipient, the subject, the body and the signature.
